summary: 66-year-old woman with moderate COPD: 2 days of more cough and white sputum, mildly more breathless; SpO₂ 94 % (her baseline), RR 20, afebrile. GOLD 2025: short-acting bronchodilators at home; antibiotics only for purulent sputum.

inputs.hpi: Moderate COPD. Two days of more coughing and more white sputum after her grandson's cold; a little more breathless on hills. Sputum not discoloured. Sleeping normally. Follow-up after laparoscopic umbilical hernia repair (healed).

exam.respiratory: Scattered expiratory wheeze, no crackles, RR 20.

surgicalHistory: Laparoscopic umbilical hernia repair (6 weeks ago)

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Mild exacerbation of COPD
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Mild COPD exacerbation (non-purulent sputum, SpO2 at baseline): increase salbutamol, safety-net; antibiotics not indicated.

guideline.name: GOLD 2025 report - Global strategy for the prevention, diagnosis and management of COPD
guideline.section: Chapter 5 exacerbations: controlled oxygen to SpO2 88-92%; arterial blood gas; non-invasive ventilation for acute respiratory acidosis (PaCO2 >=6.0 kPa / 45 mmHg and pH <=7.35); short-acting bronchodilators; systemic corticosteroids (prednisone 40 mg/day for 5 days); antibiotics when sputum purulence increases
guideline.citation: Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease. GOLD 2025 report. www.goldcopd.org.

guideline.name: BTS guideline for oxygen use in healthcare and emergency settings
guideline.section: Target SpO2 94-98% for most acutely ill patients; 88-92% for patients at risk of hypercapnic respiratory failure (e.g. COPD) pending blood gases
guideline.citation: O'Driscoll BR, Howard LS, Earis J, Mak V. Thorax. 2017;72(Suppl 1):ii1-90.

rationale: Over-triage / over-treatment control for the COPD base case.
